note: A screen, not an audit: questions worth asking and the data needed to answer them. No savings are computed; typical benefits are the cited sources' general wording.

questions.question: Which measurements have no controller (read by people, or by nothing)?

evidence.text: instrument PT-B reads "PT-B Supplied fictional instrument" at U-A
no controller in the model or loop list reads these measurements

data_requests.item: Whether operators adjust anything by hand from these readings
where: site records: operator logs and round sheets
ask the operators which of these they act on, and how often
data_requests.how: Note manual adjustments per shift tied to each reading.

data_requests.item: The control system's own loop list
where: DCS/PLC configuration: export the loop and point list
data_requests.how: Confirm the reading is indication-only and not read by logic the model lacks.

questions.decision_rule: Worth automating a reading that operators adjust by hand often, on a service where steadier control saves energy or quality; indication-only readings nobody acts on close the question.

typical_benefit.wording: "energy and cost savings are around 5% or more for many industrial applications of process control systems" (for plants without updated controls). Process control: "Typically 2-18% savings." The source says these figures "cannot be added".
source_titles: S19: Worrell & Galitsky, Energy Efficiency Improvement and Cost Saving Opportunities for Petroleum Refineries: An ENERGY STAR Guide (LBNL-56183, Feb 2005)

questions.limits: The model or loop list may be incomplete; an uncontrolled reading may be read by logic not in the model.
